quote.text: There are no shortcuts to any place worth going.
quote.author: Beverly Sills, the American soprano (1929–2007)

stories.headline: A Ryokan That Books the Sea Into Every Room
stories.dek: Hoshino's newest onsen ryokan, KAI Miyajima, opens this summer on the water at Miyajimaguchi — fifty-four rooms, every one facing the sea, looking across to the floating torii of Itsukushima. After the Nara prison stay we flagged last week, this is the escape without the provocation: no concept to argue with, just the tide and the gate.

stories.headline: The Spare-Room Brewery
stories.dek: Four ingredients, three weeks of patience, and a shed full of stainless steel: home beer making is the hobby that turns a kitchen into a small factory and never, honestly, saves anyone money. It is also a hobby in retreat — its flagship club has halved since 2019 — which makes now a good time to look at what the diehards actually do down there.

stories.headline: A Corridor With a Price, and Still No Ship
stories.dek: The Hormuz lane finally has a name attached to it: Iran and Oman say they have agreed a "temporary route." Read the small print and it is a toll road built to last two-to-four months, running mostly through Iranian water, that its own author says is not a reopening. The announcement moved the oil price; no hull has moved through it.

stories.headline: The Parade Came Home; the Policy Comes Later
stories.dek: For the first time in a decade the National Day Parade returned to the National Stadium — a covered arena, twice the seats, a first-ever indoor drone show, and a theme, "Go Beyond." What it cost to strip out the Red Lions and the flypast was the parade's own military signature. And the policy the country actually needs still waits a fortnight, for the Rally.

stories.headline: A Record Number of Million-Dollar Flats, in a Falling Market
stories.dek: The headline resale index has now dropped for a second straight quarter — yet over those very months a record 491 public-housing flats sold for seven figures each. Both are true. For an owner weighing when to sell and when to wait, the two-speed market is the only number that matters, and it is not the one on the front page.

stories.headline: Meta Ships the Closed One; the Open One Is Still a Week Away
stories.dek: The week's real frontier news came from Meta, which released a coding model and its first agent — powerful, and firmly shut. The open-weights prize everyone actually wants, Alibaba's Max-class Qwen checkpoint, was promised for this coming week and has not landed. The contrast is the story: what ships is closed, and what is open is still a date.

stories.headline: The Order Page Opens Tuesday; the Reviews Do Not
stories.dek: Insta360 turns its X6 teaser into a live deposit on 12 August — dual one-inch sensors, 8K, record-the-room-and-crop-later. For a buy-once buyer the sum is simple and unwelcome: the deposit is available days before any verdict is, so the disciplined move is to sit on your hands.

stories.headline: Spider-Man Holds — and We Owe You a Correction
stories.dek: The reboot dropped about 60% in weekend two and still posted one of the biggest second weekends ever. But the record we printed last week was wrong: the opening was the second-biggest domestic ever, not the first. We keep score on ourselves, so here is the fix — and, on Friday, Phoebe Bridgers.

stories.headline: What You Know Beats What You Block
stories.dek: A 2026 study finds that a parent's open awareness of what a child does online curbs bedtime screen use more reliably than any parental-control app. The lever, again, is not a lock on the device — it is a relationship with the child using it. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: The Whole Book Waits on Tuesday
stories.dek: A week after payrolls went negative, the repricing has settled into a coin-flip: the market has killed the rate hike but not yet bought a cut. Everything now hinges on Tuesday's inflation print. A hot number over a cracking jobs market is the stagflation box; a soft one opens the door. And a correction to last week's book: gold's move was a seven-week high, not a record.

stories.headline: The Shortcut Has a Muscle Bill
stories.dek: New data on the weight-loss drugs adds an awkward finding to a known problem: people losing weight on GLP-1s move less, not more — exactly the wrong behaviour when up to 45% of the weight coming off is muscle. The earned version of the same goal is unglamorous and well-evidenced: a barbell twice a week and a protein target. Not medical advice.

stories.headline: The Tax at the Till, and the Suite You Can't Board From Here
stories.dek: Two Japan clocks matter to a Singapore flyer: the departure tax has already tripled, and from November the country ends walk-out tax-free shopping — the friction a camera-buyer will actually feel. Meanwhile the world's largest business seat enters service this month, on the one hub a Changi traveller can't reach it from.

stories.headline: What's Worth Booking
stories.dek: Seats for the Tokyo autumn sumo tournament went on sale this weekend, and the good ones empty within hours. Beyond it, a packed Singapore quarter fronted by the Grand Prix's first-ever Sprint weekend.

stories.headline: Vietnam Builds an Idol Factory
stories.dek: Two years ago Vietnam imported its pop spectacle — Blackpink filled a Hanoi stadium and left. Now it manufactures its own: home-grown survival shows minting domestic idols, stadium tours selling out in forty-five minutes, and a government writing "the concert economy" into its plan for GDP. It is South Korea's Hallyu playbook, run in fast-forward — and the West has not noticed.
